subject: Community Preservation Act FY2018 Funding Round
overview: The Community Preservation Committee held an information session to detail the eligibility requirements, strategic goals, and application timeline for the upcoming $1.4 million funding cycle. The presentation explained how funds are distributed across open space, historic preservation, and affordable housing categories.

items.title: Introduction to the CPA and Committee Structure
items.summary: Danielle Evans explained the state program's role in funding open space, affordable housing, and historic preservation through a local 1.5% property tax surcharge.

items.title: Funding Sources and Revenue Projections
items.summary: The committee reported expected FY2018 revenue of over $1.4 million, including a 17.2% match from the state trust fund.

items.title: Small Grants Program and Funding Allocations
items.summary: The program aims for an even distribution of funds across three main categories and provides a streamlined process for small grants up to $5,000.

items.title: Eligibility and Partnership Requirements
items.summary: Eligible applicants include city departments, registered organizations, and individuals, though projects on city property require a formal municipal partner.

items.title: Application Process and Approval Steps
items.summary: The process begins with an eligibility determination before moving to a full application, public presentation, and final approval by the City Council.

items.title: Project Categories and Evaluation Criteria
items.summary: Potential projects are evaluated based on their alignment with the Community Preservation Plan, public benefit, and readiness to proceed.

items.title: Strategic Goals for Funding Categories
items.summary: The coordinator outlined specific goals for open space, recreation, affordable housing, and historic preservation as defined by public input.

items.title: Round Two Application Timeline
items.summary: Key deadlines include eligibility forms due April 13, full applications due July 13, and anticipated grant awards in November.
